rendered: The premise is not quite right: the authors did not use a carbonate electrolyte. They used NaPF6 salt dissolved in tetraglyme[1], a glyme-based electrolyte, and they chose it in contrast to traditional organic carbonate electrolytes[2]. The stated reason is the sodium anode's SEI: the glyme was chosen to overcome the unstable SEI formation on Na metal anodes observed in carbonate-based electrolytes[3][4]. Building on earlier work, the glyme supports sodium anode stability during reversible plating. This stable anode-electrolyte interface is what the authors describe as critical to good cycling performance.[5][6]
